title: Shortcuts to Adiabaticity for non-Hermitian systems in Krylov Space
authors: Ankit W. Shrestha, Budhaditya Bhattacharjee, Adolfo del Campo
abstract: Shortcuts to adiabaticity (STA) reproduce adiabatic dynamics in finite time, but their counterdiabatic implementation relies on the adiabatic gauge potential (AGP), which is difficult to compute and implement in many-body systems and whose extension to open and non-Hermitian settings has remained largely model-specific. Here, we develop a general, diagonalization-free framework for engineering STA in non-Hermitian systems by representing the AGP in Krylov space. Starting from an integral representation of the counterdiabatic control, we recast the AGP as a nested-commutator series with controlled locality and generate the associated Krylov basis using the bi-Lanczos and Arnoldi algorithms. This reduces the exact or truncated AGP to a sparse tridiagonal or upper-Hessenberg matrix equation that generalizes the Hermitian construction. We demonstrate the method on a decaying two-level atom, where it recovers the exact drive and signals the exceptional point; on the interacting Hatano-Nelson model, where truncated controls rapidly suppress nonadiabatic excitations; and on a PT-symmetric Heisenberg chain, whose AGP norm detects the PT-symmetry-breaking transition. Throughout, the expansion converges with only a small fraction of the full Krylov space, offering a practical route to fast, accurate control of many-body non-Hermitian systems.
summary: This paper introduces a general, diagonalization-free method to calculate the Adiabatic Gauge Potential (AGP) required for Shortcuts to Adiabaticity in non-Hermitian quantum systems. By mapping the problem onto Krylov space using bi-Lanczos and Arnoldi algorithms, it reduces complex calculations to sparse matrix equations. This provides an accurate and practical route for controlling dynamics and diagnosing phase transitions in challenging many-body models.
main_problem: The core problem is developing a general, computationally feasible framework for engineering Shortcuts to Adiabaticity (STA) in complex non-Hermitian quantum systems.
main_result: The authors successfully recast the difficult-to-compute Adiabatic Gauge Potential (AGP) into a sparse matrix equation solvable via Krylov space methods, applicable across various non-Hermitian models.
method: They utilize an integral representation of the counterdiabatic control and generate the necessary basis using bi-Lanczos and Arnoldi algorithms to reduce the AGP calculation to manageable linear algebra problems.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to general non-Hermitian quantum systems, demonstrated on specific models like decaying two-level atoms, the interacting Hatano-Nelson model, and PT-symmetric Heisenberg chains.
key_observables: Adiabatic Gauge Potential (AGP) norm, which serves as a diagnostic tool for detecting phase transitions like PT-symmetry breaking.
important_parameters: The tuning parameter $\lambda$ governing the system's evolution; convergence relies on only a small fraction of the full Krylov space.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that representing the AGP in the Krylov basis provides a practical and accurate alternative to direct diagonalization, even for complex many-body Hamiltonians.
figures_summary: Not specified by notes; the method involves deriving recurrence relations and solving matrix equations derived from bi-Lanczos/Arnoldi procedures.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the challenge of STA in non-Hermitian settings, developing the general Krylov space framework using integral representations, detailing the algorithmic implementation (bi-Lanczos/Arnoldi), and concluding with physical demonstrations on multiple model systems.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful computational tool to analyze non-adiabatic dynamics and phase transitions in open or non-Hermitian quantum systems, which are central topics in modern AMO physics and condensed matter theory.
